title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for knee osteoarthritis.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on RA, Temp 98.4 F, Weight 145 lbs.

Recent Labs: Hemoglobin 12.4 g/dL, White Blood Cell Count 7.2 x 10^3/uL, Sodium 138 mEq/L, Potassium 4.1 mEq/L.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, fatigue.
Eyes: No vision changes.
Ears/Nose/Throat: No congestion, no hearing loss.
Respiratory: Denies shortness of breath, cough.
Cardiovascular: No chest pain, no palpitations.
Gastrointestinal: No abdominal pain, no diarrhea.
Musculoskeletal: Positive for bilateral knee pain, stiffness in the morning.
Neurological: No dizziness, no numbness.
Skin: No rashes.

Social History: Retired. Lives at home with her daughter. Independent with ADLs. Non-smoker.

Family History: Mother had osteoarthritis. Father had a history of heart disease.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is an 85-year-old female presenting for evaluation of chronic knee osteoarthritis. She reports bilateral knee pain that is exacerbated by walking and climbing stairs. She notes occasional stiffness in the morning that improves with movement. She denies any recent falls or acute traumatic injuries. She currently manages symptoms with activity modification.

Medication List: 
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Furosemide 20mg daily
- Acetaminophen 500mg every 6 hours as needed for pain

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert and oriented x3. In no acute distress.
Musculoskeletal: Bilateral knees show mild swelling and tenderness over the patellar area. Decreased range of motion noted on flexion of the right knee. No joint instability. Gait is steady.

Problem List:
- Chronic systolic heart failure
- Status post appendectomy
- Status post cholecystectomy
- Knee osteoarthritis

Assessment:
1. Knee Osteoarthritis: The patient’s symptoms are currently stable. She reports mild discomfort but is maintaining her activity level.
2. Chronic systolic heart failure: Symptoms reviewed; patient is stable on current medications.

Plan:
1. Knee Osteoarthritis: Continue current conservative management. Encourage gentle stretching and aquatic therapy.
2. Chronic systolic heart failure: Continue current medication regimen including Furosemide and Lisinopril. Will monitor for any signs of fluid retention.

Electronically signed, 
D. Kowalski, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: The provider addressed chronic systolic heart failure at this visit, so it is supported: I50.22.

distractors.why: Status plus a plan in the assessment supports the diagnosis.
